review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped for every simp attribute and every `simp`/`rw` use of the bridge lemmas. I also read the core `show ... from` elaborator to see what term it produces. Simp use in this file is almost entirely `simp only [...]`. The `@[scoped simp]` lemmas (`fn₁_*`, `ofFun_toFun'`, `fstHom_app`, `sndHom_app`, `mulFrameHom_app`, `subPresheaf_map_apply_val`) are never fired by a plain `simp` here. Their downstream effect in other files is uncertain. The findings are interface-quality concerns, not observed simplifier failures. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about loops or failures. I found no competing rules, no rewrite loops and no wrong-direction rules.

findings.declaration: fn₁_zero, fn₁_add, fn₁_smul, fn₁_map (and the fn₂ analogues); ofFun_toFun'
findings.excerpt: @[scoped simp] lemma fn₁_add (W : (XT).Opens) (f g : Γ(P¹, W)) : fn₁ W (f + g) = fn₁ W f + fn₁ W g := rfl
findings.problem: The scoped simp set for the identity-cast bridge `fn₁`/`fn₂` is only partly tagged. The simp set contains `fn₁_ofFn₁`, `fn₁_zero` and `fn₁_add`. The equally rfl, equally push-inward lemmas `fn₁_smul` and `fn₁_map` have no simp attribute. After `simp` pushes `fn₁` through `+`, it stalls at `r • f` and at restriction maps. The file works around this by hand. `nodeFamily_zero` uses `rw [fn₁_zero, fn₂_zero, map_zero, map_zero, mul_zero]`. `nodeFamily_add` uses `rw [fn₁_add, fn₂_add, map_add, map_add, mul_add, ...]`. `nodeFamily_smul` uses `rw [fn₁_smul, fn₂_smul, ...]`. The simp attributes on the other lemmas are therefore not used. Round-trip lemmas are also one-sided. `ofFun_toFun'` is simp and `fn₁_ofFn₁` is simp, but there is no `toFun'_ofFun` or `ofFn₁_fn₁`. `conductor` relies on defeq in `exact congrArg (toFun' W) e` to get back from `ofFun W r = ofFun W r'` to `r = r'`.
findings.proposed_change: Make the family uniform. Either tag `fn₁_smul`, `fn₂_smul`, `fn₁_map`, `fn₂_map` as `@[scoped simp]` too, so simp pushes `fn` to `(i₁T).app W r * fn₁ W f` and to the restriction map on `C₁T`. Or drop the simp attribute from the zero/add lemmas so the interface is not misleadingly partial. Add the missing `toFun'_ofFun` (rfl, scoped simp) next to `ofFun_toFun'`. Then `simp` could replace the explicit `rw` chains and the final `congrArg (toFun' W) e`.
findings.benefit: A single canonical normal form (`fn` pushed to atoms) lets `simp` close `NodeCondition` goals about `fn₁ W (…)` directly. The proofs in `nodeFamily_*` and `conductor` no longer need hand-ordered `rw` lists. Both round-trip directions for the cast pairs are covered.

findings.excerpt: (fstHom hS).app W m = (show subMod hS W from m).1.1 := rfl
findings.problem: These scoped simp lemmas state their right-hand side with `show subMod hS W from m`. The core `show … from` elaborator builds a `have`-wrapped term to force the type syntactically. The simp-lemma RHS therefore contains a `have this : subMod hS W := m; this` redex instead of a plain `m.1.1`. A simp rule's RHS is the intended normal form, and it should not carry such a redex. It also shows that the lemma is stated on a type (`Γ(subModule hS, W)`) whose projections are not directly available. The companion `mem_subMod` (line 65, `p ∈ subMod hS W ↔ p ∈ S W := Iff.rfl`) is not simp. `subMod` is a plain `def`, so simp cannot see through it. This is why `exists_injective_and_range_eq` writes `(show subMod hS W from m).2` and `⟨p, hp⟩` by hand.
findings.proposed_change: State the lemmas with a binder `(m : subMod hS W)`, so the RHS is the clean `m.1.1` / `m.1.2`. Tag `mem_subMod` with `@[scoped simp]`, or keep it as a separately named rw lemma. The `show` ascriptions in `exists_injective_and_range_eq` would then be unnecessary.
findings.benefit: The simp normal form is a plain projection, with no `have` redex. Membership in `subMod` can be unfolded by simp in the same scoped set. Proofs about `subModule` no longer need `show` casts.

findings.excerpt: @[scoped simp] lemma mulFrameHom_app (W : U.toScheme.Opens) (g : Γ(X, U.ι ''ᵁ W)) :
findings.problem: `mulFrameHom_app` rewrites `(mulFrameHom m₀).app W g` to `mulFrame m₀ W g`. `mulFrame` is an opaque `def` whose body is `g • resFrame m₀ W`. Its algebra lemmas `mulFrame_add`, `mulFrame_mul` and `mulFrame_map` have no simp attribute and are only used via `rw`/`erw`. The simp lemma therefore leads simp to a term it cannot simplify further. In particular, `mulFrameHom_app` followed by `g + g'`, `r * g` or `0` stays stuck at `mulFrame`. The scoped simp lemma has no companion rules and is not exercised in the file; `isIso_mulFrameHom` goes through `bijective_mulFrame`.
findings.proposed_change: Either add `mulFrame_add` and a `mulFrame_zero` as simp lemmas, so the `mulFrame` normal form is a complete interface. Or state `mulFrameHom_app` with the unfolded form `g • resFrame m₀ W` and tag that, so simp can use the existing `add_smul`, `mul_smul` and `zero_smul`. Otherwise drop the attribute.
findings.benefit: Either option gives a rewrite target that simp can keep normalizing, instead of a dead end at the `mulFrame` definition. Users of `mulFrameHom` no longer need manual `unfold mulFrame`.
